_schema: Seed data for verb intake 2026-07-07. pres = base verb present forms [ich,du,er,wir,ihr,sie]. praet = 6 forms or ich-form string (regular). sep = separable prefix or null. sent: p = person key or 'inf'. Answers with 'X ... Y' mark separable split.

sent.en: I connect the two cables.
The bridge connects the two districts.

sent.de: Er _____ mit diesem Lied schöne Erinnerungen.
sent.en: He associates beautiful memories with this song.

roots.trans_note: Inseparable — 'ver' never detaches.

gram.notes_en: verbinden takes a direct object in the accusative: 'Ich verbinde die Kabel.' Use 'mit' + Dativ for 'connect with': 'Ich verbinde den Drucker mit dem Computer.'

roots.english: to please / to be pleasing to

sent.en: I like the book a lot (the book pleases me).
My mother likes the new furniture.
How do you like the apartment?

roots.trans_note: The thing that pleases is the subject; the person goes in the dative.

gram.notes_en: gefallen takes the dative for the person: 'Das Buch gefällt MIR.' The thing that pleases is the grammatical subject — the opposite of English 'I like the book'.

sent.de: Ich _____ Mehl und Zucker in einer Schüssel.
sent.en: I mix flour and sugar in a bowl.
The bartender mixes the cocktails.
You are mixing the colours too dark.

roots.trans_note: Regular weak verb.

gram.notes_en: mischen takes an accusative object: 'Ich mische die Zutaten.'

sent.de: Ich _____ die Zutaten mit einem Löffel.
sent.en: I blend the ingredients with a spoon.

sent.de: Man darf diese zwei Begriffe nicht _____.
sent.en: One must not mix up these two concepts.
He often mixes up reality and fantasy.

variants.notes: Inseparable prefix: Ich vermische die Farben. Often figurative: Begriffe/Themen vermischen.

sent.de: Ich _____ mit dem Verkäufer über den Preis.
sent.en: I negotiate the price with the seller.
The union is negotiating higher wages.

sent.de: Wir _____ seit Wochen mit der Bank.
sent.en: We have been negotiating with the bank for weeks.

roots.trans_note: -eln verb: ich verhandle (the e drops).

gram.notes_en: verhandeln is used with 'mit' + Dativ (partner) and 'über' + Akkusativ (topic): 'Wir verhandeln mit der Firma über den Vertrag.'

sent.en: I am developing a new app.
The company develops eco-friendly products.
Children develop their language very quickly.

roots.trans_note: Inseparable — no ge- in the Partizip II: entwickelt.

gram.notes_en: entwickeln takes an accusative object. Reflexive 'sich entwickeln' = to develop/evolve (by itself): 'Die Stadt entwickelt sich schnell.'

roots.english: to take care of / to get done

sent.en: I'll take care of the shopping today.
My colleague takes care of that immediately.
You'll get that done later, right?

roots.trans_note: Inseparable — no ge- in the Partizip II: erledigt.

gram.notes_en: erledigen takes an accusative object: 'Ich erledige die Aufgabe.' Very common for chores, errands and tasks.

sent.en: I strive for a better life.
He strives for perfection.
Many people strive for success.

roots.trans_note: Almost always with 'nach' + Dativ.

gram.notes_en: streben is used with 'nach' + Dativ: 'Er strebt nach Erfolg.' The dative comes from the preposition nach.

sent.de: Ich _____ mich am Wochenende meiner Familie.
sent.en: On weekends I devote myself to my family.

sent.de: Der Autor _____ das Buch seiner Frau.
sent.en: The author dedicates the book to his wife.
She devotes herself entirely to her profession.

roots.trans_note: Stem ends in -m: du widmest, er widmet.

gram.notes_en: widmen takes accusative (the thing) + dative (the receiver): 'Er widmet ihr (Dat) das Buch (Akk).' Reflexive 'sich widmen' + Dativ = to devote oneself to something.

roots.english: to shape / to characterize / to coin (a term)

sent.en: Childhood shapes our character.
These experiences shape me to this day.

sent.de: Der Trainer _____ den Stil der Mannschaft.
sent.en: The coach shapes the team's style.

roots.trans_note: Common in texts about influence: eine Epoche/Person prägen.

gram.notes_en: prägen takes an accusative object: 'Der Krieg prägte eine ganze Generation.' Also: einen Begriff prägen = to coin a term.

sent.en: I publish my photos on the internet.

sent.de: Der Verlag _____ zehn neue Bücher pro Jahr.
sent.en: The publisher publishes ten new books per year.
When are you publishing your article?

roots.trans_note: Inseparable — no ge- in the Partizip II: veröffentlicht.

gram.notes_en: veröffentlichen takes an accusative object: 'Sie veröffentlicht einen Roman.' Passive is very common: 'Das Buch wird veröffentlicht.'

sent.en: I sweep the yard every Saturday.

sent.de: Er _____ die Blätter von der Terrasse.
sent.en: He sweeps the leaves off the terrace.
You never sweep the kitchen!

roots.trans_note: Also figurative in fixed phrases: den Rücken kehren (to turn one's back).

gram.notes_en: kehren (to sweep) takes an accusative object. In its 'turn' sense it appears mostly in fixed phrases and in the separable verb zurückkehren (to return).

sent.en: I return to Germany next week.

sent.de: Er _____ nach dem Studium in seine Heimat _____.
sent.en: He returns to his home country after his studies.
When do you (pl.) return from holiday?

variants.notes: Separable: Ich kehre morgen zurück. Uses 'sein' in the Perfekt: Ich bin zurückgekehrt.

sent.de: Ich _____ gern zum Erfolg des Projekts _____.
sent.en: I gladly contribute to the project's success.
Everyone can contribute something to environmental protection.
Sport contributes to health.

roots.trans_note: Separable: the prefix 'bei' detaches — 'Ich trage bei.'

gram.notes_en: beitragen is used with 'zu' + Dativ: 'Das trägt zur Lösung bei.' The dative comes from the preposition zu.

sent.en: I often argue with my brother.
The neighbours argue about the fence.
Why are you (pl.) arguing again?

roots.trans_note: Often reflexive: sich streiten (mit jemandem, über etwas).

gram.notes_en: streiten is usually reflexive: 'Wir streiten uns.' Partner with 'mit' + Dativ, topic with 'über' + Akkusativ.

roots.english: to be enough / to hand (something to someone)

sent.de: Das Geld _____ nicht für den Urlaub.
sent.en: The money is not enough for the holiday.
I hand you the salt.
Are two hours enough for the task?

roots.trans_note: Don't confuse with riechen (to smell)!

gram.notes_en: In the sense 'to be enough', the person is in the dative: 'Das reicht mir.' In the sense 'to hand', it takes dative + accusative: 'Ich reiche dir (Dat) das Buch (Akk).'

sent.en: I smell fresh coffee.
The food smells very good.
Do you smell that too?

roots.trans_note: Don't confuse with reichen (to be enough)!

gram.notes_en: riechen can take an accusative object ('Ich rieche Rauch') or stand alone with 'nach' + Dativ: 'Es riecht nach Kaffee.'

sent.de: Viele Familien _____ jedes Jahr nach Kanada _____.
sent.en: Many families immigrate to Canada every year.
He is immigrating to Australia next year.
Why don't you just immigrate?

roots.trans_note: Separable. Opposite: auswandern (to emigrate).

gram.notes_en: einwandern is intransitive and uses 'sein' in the Perfekt: 'Sie ist nach Deutschland eingewandert.' Related noun: die Einwanderung.

sent.en: I always express my opinion clearly.

sent.de: Man kann Dankbarkeit auch ohne Worte _____.
sent.en: One can express gratitude without words too.

sent.de: Sie _____ ihre Freude mit einem Lächeln _____.
sent.en: She expresses her joy with a smile.

roots.trans_note: Separable: the prefix 'aus' detaches — 'Ich drücke es aus.'

gram.notes_en: ausdrücken takes an accusative object: 'Gefühle ausdrücken.' Reflexive 'sich ausdrücken' = to express oneself: 'Er drückt sich gut aus.'

sent.en: The storm causes great damage.
I don't want to cause any problems.
Construction sites often cause long traffic jams.

roots.trans_note: Inseparable — no ge- in the Partizip II: verursacht.

gram.notes_en: verursachen takes an accusative object: 'Der Unfall verursachte einen Stau.' Related noun: die Ursache (cause).

roots.english: to be cancelled / to slip one's mind / to be allotted to (auf)

sent.en: The course is cancelled today due to illness.
Unfortunately, the last two lectures are cancelled.
The appointment is cancelled without replacement.

roots.trans_note: Inseparable. Three meanings: cancelled; forgotten ('Der Name ist mir entfallen'); allotted ('Auf X entfällt die Hälfte').

gram.notes_en: In the sense 'to slip one's mind', the person is dative: 'Der Name ist MIR entfallen.' Uses 'sein' in the Perfekt.

roots.english: to explain in detail / to elaborate on

sent.en: I'll gladly explain the details to you.

sent.de: Der Professor _____ die Theorie an einem Beispiel.
sent.en: The professor explains the theory using an example.
Can you please explain that in more detail?

roots.trans_note: More formal and detailed than erklären.

gram.notes_en: erläutern takes accusative (the thing) and optionally dative (the person): 'Er erläutert uns (Dat) den Plan (Akk).' Stronger than erklären: implies detail and examples.

sent.en: "Finally!", she exclaims excitedly.
The government wants to declare a state of emergency.
Why are you exclaiming so loudly?

roots.trans_note: Separable: the prefix 'aus' detaches — 'Sie ruft aus.'

gram.notes_en: ausrufen takes an accusative object: 'den Notstand ausrufen', 'einen Namen ausrufen'. Very common in written narration for exclamations.

sent.en: I dispose of the old fridge properly.
How does one dispose of batteries correctly?
We dispose of our rubbish separately.

roots.trans_note: Inseparable — no ge- in the Partizip II: entsorgt.

gram.notes_en: entsorgen takes an accusative object: 'Müll entsorgen.' Related noun: die Entsorgung (waste disposal).

sent.de: Ich _____ die alten Zeitungen in den Container.
sent.en: I chuck the old newspapers into the container.
He chucks his jacket onto the sofa.

sent.de: Warum _____ du das Papier auf den Boden?
sent.en: Why are you throwing the paper on the floor?

roots.trans_note: Colloquial synonym of werfen. du/er forms are identical: schmeißt.

gram.notes_en: schmeißen takes an accusative object. Colloquial register — in formal writing use werfen. Also: eine Party schmeißen (to throw a party).

sent.en: I throw the ball to you.
The boy throws stones into the water.
Will you throw me the towel, please?

roots.trans_note: Strong verb with vowel change: du wirfst, er wirft.

gram.notes_en: werfen takes an accusative object: 'Ich werfe den Ball.' Vowel change e→i in du/er forms.

variants.english: to drop / to throw off / to yield (profit)

sent.de: Das Flugzeug _____ Hilfspakete über der Region _____.
sent.en: The plane drops aid packages over the region.
The investment is supposed to yield profit soon.

sent.de: Die Bäume _____ im Herbst ihre Blätter _____.
sent.en: The trees shed their leaves in autumn.

variants.notes: Separable: Das Flugzeug wirft die Ladung ab. Figurative: Gewinn abwerfen = to yield a profit.

sent.en: I don't throw away food.
Many people throw away too much plastic.
Why are you throwing away the shoes?

variants.notes: Separable: Ich werfe es weg. Key vocabulary in texts about waste (Lebensmittelverschwendung).

sent.de: Ich _____ zu viel Zeit mit dem Handy.
sent.en: I waste too much time on my phone.

sent.de: Wir _____ jeden Tag Wasser und Energie.
sent.en: We waste water and energy every day.
He is wasting his talent.

roots.trans_note: Don't confuse with verschwinden (to disappear).

gram.notes_en: verschwenden takes an accusative object: 'Zeit/Geld/Energie verschwenden.' Related noun: die Verschwendung (waste).
